newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere sees Thomson deal EPS positive.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere sees Thomson deal EPS positive.

text.p: French conglomerate Lagardere Groupe said on Wednesday the planned merger of its Matra unit with defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF would lead to sustained growth in net profit per share for Lagardere.

"The shareholders of Lagardere will benefit from this acquisition thanks to...the synergies flowing from the merger of Thomson CSF-Matra, through durable growth in net profit per share (before goodwill amortisation) for Lagardere," Lagardere said in a statement.
Lagardere plans to merge its Matra Defense Espace unit with Thomson-CSF to create Thomson Matra and has offered to buy out CSF minorities at 156 francs per share.
Thomson Matra would be 60 percent owned by Lagardere and would be quoted on the stock market.

The French government earlier said it preferred Lagardere's bid for Thomson SA, parent of Thomson-CSF, as it had a better industrial logic than rival Alcatel Alsthom. The two bids are being referred to the Privatisation Commission for consideration. The commission is expected to support the government's choice.
